title: service-automation test: the sealed-envelope pin fails when random ciphertext happens to contain the fixture connector name `crm`
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cyvF7SP65frVFAYLv7

Filing gate: ① a defect with a named location and a reproduction: a probabilistic flake in a CI test. Per the dispatch rule 「谁发现 flake 谁修或立单」, the seat that met it files it. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested grade: p3.
Business reason: about once in a thousand runs, `Test Core` goes red on unrelated PRs, and the seat re-runs it. This costs merge-queue time and seat attention, and a real red can be dismissed as "that flake".
Reader who acts: `domain:server` (`packages/services/service-automation`), test only.
Dedupe (`is:issue`): `authorization.test.ts flake` 1 hit (#20594, unrelated); `sealed envelope crm` 36 (none on this test); `oauth2-grant authorization test` 21 (ADR and connector cards, none on this test). **New.**

## Reproduction

PR #30952 (touches `packages/rest` only), run 42230858051, job `Test Core (7/8)`, head `3bccb0f7`:

```
src/oauth2-grant/authorization.test.ts:138
ADR-0143 D5 — a begun connect is held sealed (the KV trust boundary)
  > the KV holds no verifier, user, organization, instance or redirect URI — only an envelope
AssertionError: expected '{"v":1,"iv":"eXrbrlZgkO7ZUjQf","ct":"…gpcrmVS1…' not to contain 'crm'
```

## Why

The pin JSON-stringifies the stored envelope `{ v, iv, ct, tag }` and asserts that it does not contain each plaintext field. One of those fields is `begun.connector`, which the `pending()` fixture sets to `'crm'` (L22). The `iv`, `ct` and `tag` fields are random base64url. A random string of about 230 base64url characters contains a given three-character run in roughly 1 run in 1,100. `org_a` and `usr_1` are short too, at lower odds.

## Expected

- The pin no longer depends on luck. Either give the fixture's plaintext fields values that cannot plausibly occur in base64url output (for example a connector name of 12 or more characters that includes a character base64url never emits), or assert on the decoded envelope structure (only `v`, `iv`, `ct`, `tag`) plus a check that a decryption with the wrong key yields nothing.
- The pin still goes red if the store writes any plaintext field. Ablate once.
- Test only, so no changeset.
